flares.teff_fallback: when TIC v8.2 has no Teff, the CHEOPS archive's target record (DACE teff_k), labelled as such

pulsations.tolerance: strict: 3 × the combined frequency uncertainty (ours and published, Montgomery & O'Donoghue); loose: the Rayleigh resolution 1/T

checks.text: AU Mic S1: recall of Günther et al. (2020) flares, 95% interval lower bound ≥ 0.70
AU Mic S1: flux-inverted null finds at most 1 event per 10 days
Proxima S11-12: recall of Medina et al. (2020) flares with ED ≥ 3 s, every bin's 95% interval lower bound ≥ 0.5
Proxima S11-12: at least 85% of our flares are in Medina et al.'s list
TIC 150359500: our 9000 K bolometric energies within a factor 1.5 of Günther et al.'s (median ratio's 95% interval inside [0.67, 1.5])
Quiet stars: fewer than 0.02 detections per day
CHEOPS DRP M dwarfs (denoised): complex fraction's 95% interval contains Poyatos et al.'s ≈ 0.42
CHEOPS DRP M dwarfs (denoised): power-law index within 2σ (combined) of Poyatos et al.'s 1.99 ± 0.10
β Pic S5-7: the 10 strongest of Zieba et al.'s (2019) frequencies all recovered within 3σ
β Pic S5-7: at least 80% of the 54 published frequencies within the Rayleigh resolution
HR 10 S2 and S29: the 10 strongest of Salmon et al.'s (2024) frequencies recovered within 1/T in both sectors
HR 10 S2 and S29: at least 80% of the published frequencies within 1/T
TOI-197 S2: numax and Δν within 2σ of Huber et al. (2019)
HR 10 S29 residual: AR(1) surrogates give fewer than 1 false frequency per light curve on average
Same input as pycheops: our decorrelation matches pycheops' to < 10 ppm rms on every reference visit
End to end (DACE DRP light curve vs pycheops' DRP product): correlation ≥ 0.9 on every reference visit
HR 10 CHEOPS, three public visits together: the two strongest TESS δ Scuti frequencies (f1, f2) found

unvalidated: Flare energies on stars whose TIC entry has no Teff (AU Mic and Proxima Cen in TIC v8.2): reported as unavailable.
GJ 1243: no machine-readable per-flare TESS catalogue was found; detections are reported, not compared.
GJ 65: no per-flare table is public for Bruno et al. (2024); only an internal 120 s vs 20 s check.

Poyatos et al. (2025) worked on 3-s CHEOPS imagettes reduced with PIPE; DACE serves DRP subarray light curves (about 42 s and longer), so the CHEOPS comparison is of aggregate numbers on different data products, not flare by flare. Their per-flare catalogue is not public.
Bruno et al. (2024): no per-flare catalogue; their complex fraction (≳ 30%) is quoted for context only.
Wavelet denoising: tuned and checked by injection on SetuHQ's own data; Poyatos et al.'s optimal parameters were found on imagettes and are not reproduced here.
HR 10 CHEOPS frequencies: Salmon et al. (2024) publish no CHEOPS frequency list; only the TESS lists are compared.

aumic_gunther.energies: TIC v8.2 has no Teff for AU Mic; ours use the CHEOPS archive's Teff (labelled). Günther et al. give no energies for AU Mic, so there is nothing to compare them with

energy_basis.method: Planck spectrum at the TIC Teff through the instrument response, 4πR²·π∫R B_λ dλ

beta_pic.reference: Zieba et al. 2019, A&A 625, L13 (Transiting exocomets detected in broadband light by TESS in the beta Pictoris system), Appendix table
beta_pic.reference_data: TESS sectors 5-7 PDCSAP (sector 4 excluded), Period04 pre-whitening to S/N 4 (Breger et al. 1993)

type.label: δ Scuti
reasons: 45 independent frequencies at ≥ 5 d⁻¹ (100% of the amplitude), 0 below
Teff 8000 K is inside the δ Scuti/γ Doradus range (6300-8800 K)
alternatives: a contaminating pulsator in the aperture

beta_pic.note: Zieba et al. excluded sector 4; so do we. Amplitudes: theirs in mmag, ours in relative flux.

cheops_flares.data: CHEOPS DRP (subarray) light curves via DACE public mode; Poyatos et al. used 3-s imagettes reduced with PIPE, which DACE does not serve

hr10_cheops.note: Salmon et al. used PIPE photometry of the 3-s imagettes (67 ppm per minute); DACE serves the DRP subarray light curve (42 s). They publish no CHEOPS frequency list, so ours is compared with their TESS sector 29 list.

hr10_tess.reference: Salmon et al. 2024, A&A 690, A73 (HR 10 as seen by CHEOPS and TESS), Tables A.1 and A.2
hr10_tess.reference_data: TESS sectors 2 and 29, 2-min, SAP flux corrected with CBVs (Nardiello et al. 2020 recipe); FELIX pre-whitening to S/N 5.0 (their 4-sigma level), local noise = median in a window of 300 x the resolution

type.label: hybrid δ Scuti/γ Doradus
reasons: 10 independent frequencies at ≥ 5 d⁻¹ (63% of the amplitude), 3 below
Teff 8840 K is outside the δ Scuti/γ Doradus range (6300-8800 K)

type.label: hybrid δ Scuti/γ Doradus
reasons: 12 independent frequencies at ≥ 5 d⁻¹ (73% of the amplitude), 3 below
Teff 8840 K is outside the δ Scuti/γ Doradus range (6300-8800 K)
alternatives: δ Scuti with rotational modulation or combination frequencies at low frequency
a contaminating pulsator in the aperture

granulation.note: Salmon et al. fit one Harvey component to an averaged periodogram (25 one-day series); we fit one or two to the full periodogram by maximum likelihood

quiet_stars.note: Quiet solar-type stars are not expected to show detectable white-light flares at TESS precision; every detection here counts as a false positive (an upper bound on the rate).

toi197.data_note: SetuHQ reads SPOC PDCSAP; Huber et al. used a TASOC light curve
